title: Make your mini-assistant
goal: Build and save a reusable AI helper for a job you do every week — you stay in charge of what it does.

blocks.title: Let's bottle a weekly job
blocks.body:
Pick one thing you do every single week — the Friday quiz, quick feedback lines, a worksheet starter. We're going to turn it into an assistant you keep.

First you'll write its instructions. Then you'll test it on a real topic. If it works, save it — and next week becomes a ten-second job.

blocks.brief: Write the instructions for your mini-assistant — the part you'll save and reuse. Pick one weekly job (say, a Class 7 Science quiz-maker). Give it a role, your class context, and 2–3 rules it must always follow. End with a slot for the topic that changes each week. Keep students' names and personal details out.
rubric: Names a clear role, e.g. "You are a quiz-maker for my class".
Includes your class context — grade level, subject, and board.
Lists at least two "always" rules (e.g. add an answer key, use simple English, use ₹ not $).
Leaves a slot for the part that changes each week — the topic or the text to work on.
Keeps real student names and personal details out of the prompt.

blocks.scaffold: Create a reusable assistant prompt I can save and reuse: role = a {{artifact}} for my {{gradeBand}} {{subject}} class; always follow these rules: [your 2–3 rules]; then I'll paste this week's topic. Show me the finished assistant, then test it once on this topic: [a real topic you're teaching this week].

blocks.question: You just built and tested a helper. How usable is the assistant you saved — ready for next week?
